faq.q: What is the cheapest credit card processing fee I can get in 2026?
faq.a: Based on verified public pricing as of August 2026, GoDaddy POS Plus charges 2.3% + $0 per in-person transaction — lower than Square's 2.6% + $0.15 and Stripe's 2.9% + $0.30. Some processors advertise interchange-plus pricing that can be cheaper at high volumes, but those rates are negotiated and not publicly listed. Always compare the all-in cost including monthly fees, hardware, and any per-transaction cents, not just the percentage.

faq.q: How much cheaper is GoDaddy Payments than Square per swipe?
faq.a: On a $50 in-person sale, GoDaddy POS Plus costs $1.15 (2.3% + $0), while Square costs $1.45 (2.6% + $0.15). That's $0.30 saved per transaction. At 100 transactions a day, that's roughly $900 saved per month. The gap widens on lower-ticket items because Square's $0.15 per-transaction fee hits harder on small sales.

faq.q: Does GoDaddy Payments charge a monthly fee on top of the processing rate?
faq.a: GoDaddy Payments is included with eligible GoDaddy plans. The 2.3% + $0 in-person rate applies to the POS Plus plan. Check current GoDaddy plan pricing for the monthly subscription cost, and factor that into your total cost comparison — especially if you're a low-volume merchant where a monthly fee could outweigh per-transaction savings.

faq.q: Are Helcim, Clover, Toast, and Shopify rates included in this comparison?

Rather than publish potentially outdated figures, we've marked them as unverified. Visit each provider's pricing page directly for their current rates before making a decision.

faq.q: What's the difference between a flat-rate processor and interchange-plus pricing?
faq.a: Flat-rate processors like GoDaddy, Square, and Stripe charge one predictable percentage regardless of card type. Interchange-plus pricing passes the actual card network cost to you plus a markup — it can be cheaper for high-volume merchants processing premium rewards cards, but it's harder to predict. For most small businesses doing under $500K/year in card volume, flat-rate is simpler and often competitive.

faq.q: Can I negotiate lower rates with any of these processors?
faq.a: Square and Stripe occasionally offer custom pricing for merchants processing over $250K–$500K per year. GoDaddy Payments may also have volume options — contact GoDaddy sales directly. Helcim uses interchange-plus by default, which can self-adjust lower as your volume grows. Clover and Toast rates are often set by the reseller or bank partner, so negotiation depends on who you sign with.

faq.q: Does the per-transaction cent fee really matter that much?
faq.a: Yes — especially for low-ticket merchants. If your average sale is $10, Square's $0.15 per-transaction fee adds 1.5% to your effective rate on top of the 2.6%, making the real cost 4.1%. GoDaddy's $0 per-transaction fee means your effective rate stays at 2.3% regardless of ticket size. Coffee shops, food trucks, and quick-service retailers feel this difference most.

faq.q: What happens to my processing rate if I process a keyed-in or online transaction instead of a card swipe?
faq.a: Card-not-present transactions (manually keyed, online, or phone orders) carry higher rates across all processors because fraud risk is higher. The rates in this comparison apply to in-person, card-present transactions only. Check each processor's card-not-present or online rate separately if you take orders remotely.

faq.q: Is there a way to pay 0% on credit card processing fees?
faq.a: Yes — through surcharging or cash-discount programs. GoDaddy's Rate Saver feature lets eligible merchants pass credit card fees to customers, effectively reducing your cost to 0% on credit and 1.9% + $0 on debit in-person. This is not available in Connecticut, Massachusetts, or Puerto Rico, and does not apply to ecommerce transactions. See our Rate Saver page for full details and compliance notes.

Surcharging laws vary by state and are subject to change. This page reflects known restrictions as of August 2026. Consult a legal or compliance advisor to confirm surcharging is permitted in your specific jurisdiction before enabling this feature.

Card network rules (Visa, Mastercard) require merchants to register surcharging programs and provide customer disclosure at point of entry and point of sale. GoDaddy Rate Saver handles network registration requirements for eligible merchants — confirm current registration process with GoDaddy support.
Debit card transactions cannot be surcharged under federal Durbin Amendment rules. Rate Saver applies a separate 1.9% + $0 rate to debit in-person rather than passing fees to customers.

faq.q: Can I legally charge customers a fee for paying with a credit card?
faq.a: In most U.S. states, yes — surcharging is legal as of 2026. However, it is prohibited in Connecticut and Massachusetts, and restricted in Puerto Rico. Card networks (Visa, Mastercard) also require you to register your surcharge program and disclose the fee to customers before they pay. GoDaddy Rate Saver handles the network registration piece for eligible merchants, but you are responsible for in-store disclosure signage.

faq.q: What is the difference between a surcharge and a cash discount?
faq.a: A surcharge adds a fee on top of your listed price for customers who pay by credit card. A cash discount reduces the price for customers who pay with cash, effectively building the card fee into your standard price. Both achieve a similar result — shifting processing costs to card-paying customers — but they are treated differently under state law and card network rules. Some states that prohibit surcharging still allow cash-discount programs. Consult a compliance advisor if you're in a restricted state.

faq.q: How does GoDaddy Rate Saver actually work?
faq.a: Rate Saver is a feature within GoDaddy Payments that automatically applies a customer-facing fee on credit card transactions at the point of sale, offsetting your processing cost. Your effective rate on credit card transactions drops to 0%. Debit card transactions are processed at 1.9% + $0 in-person — debit cannot be surcharged under federal law, so the cost is not fully eliminated on debit. Rate Saver is available for in-person transactions only on eligible plans.

faq.q: Does Rate Saver work for my online store?
faq.a: No. Rate Saver is currently available for in-person transactions only. It does not apply to ecommerce or online checkout transactions. If you need to reduce online processing costs, consider adjusting your product pricing or exploring other plan options.

faq.q: What states can I NOT use surcharging in?
faq.a: As of August 2026, GoDaddy Rate Saver is not available in Connecticut, Massachusetts, or Puerto Rico. These jurisdictions have laws that restrict or prohibit credit card surcharging. This list may change as state laws evolve — always verify current restrictions with a legal advisor before enabling surcharging.

faq.q: How much can I actually save with Rate Saver compared to standard processing?
faq.a: On a $100 credit card sale, standard GoDaddy POS Plus processing costs you $2.30 (2.3% + $0). With Rate Saver enabled, that $2.30 is passed to the customer as a fee, and your cost drops to $0. At $10,000/month in credit card sales, that's roughly $230/month in savings. On debit, you'd still pay 1.9% + $0 ($190/month on $10K), but the combined savings versus standard rates can be significant for high-volume merchants.

faq.q: Do I have to tell customers about the surcharge before they pay?
faq.a: Yes — card network rules require you to disclose the surcharge at the point of entry to your store or website and again at the point of sale. This typically means a sign at the door or register stating that a credit card surcharge applies. Failure to disclose can result in card network violations. GoDaddy Rate Saver displays the fee on the payment screen, but physical signage at your location is your responsibility.

faq.q: Can I surcharge debit card transactions too?
faq.a: No. Federal law (the Durbin Amendment to the Dodd-Frank Act) prohibits merchants from surcharging debit card transactions. Rate Saver applies a separate reduced rate of 1.9% + $0 to in-person debit transactions rather than passing the fee to the customer.

faq.q: What happens if a customer refuses to pay the surcharge?
faq.a: You should offer them an alternative payment method — cash, check, or debit card — at your standard price without the surcharge. Card network rules require that customers always have a surcharge-free payment option available. You cannot require all customers to pay the surcharge with no alternative.

faq.q: Is there a limit on how much I can surcharge customers?
faq.a: Yes. Visa and Mastercard cap surcharges at 3% of the transaction amount (as of 2026 network rules). You cannot surcharge more than your actual processing cost, and you cannot exceed the network cap. GoDaddy Rate Saver is designed to pass only the actual processing fee, keeping you within network compliance automatically — but confirm current network rules with GoDaddy support as caps can change.

faq.q: What's the simplest way to explain surcharging to my customers?
faq.a: Tell them upfront — at the door and at the register — that you add a small fee for credit card payments to cover your processing costs, and that they can avoid it by paying with cash or debit. Most customers understand when it's disclosed clearly and honestly. Surprise surcharges at checkout create friction and complaints; transparent disclosure upfront usually doesn't.

faq.q: Is a cash discount program the same as surcharging?
faq.a: Not exactly. With surcharging, your listed price is the base price and card-paying customers pay more. With a cash discount, your listed price already includes the card fee built in, and cash-paying customers get a discount. The end result is similar — card users effectively pay more — but the legal and disclosure treatment differs. Some states that prohibit surcharging still allow cash-discount programs, so the distinction matters depending on where you operate.

faq.q: How do I know if surcharging is legal in my state?
faq.a: As of August 2026, surcharging is prohibited in Connecticut and Massachusetts, and restricted in Puerto Rico. All other U.S. states generally permit it, subject to card network disclosure and registration requirements. State laws change, so verify current rules with a legal advisor or your state attorney general's office before enabling surcharging.

faq.q: What are the card network rules I have to follow if I surcharge?
faq.a: Visa and Mastercard require you to: (1) register your surcharge program with the card network before you start, (2) disclose the surcharge at the point of entry (e.g., store entrance) and at the point of sale, (3) cap the surcharge at your actual processing cost and no more than the network maximum (currently 3% — verify current cap), and (4) apply the surcharge consistently to all credit card transactions of that brand. You cannot surcharge only some customers or only some card types selectively.

faq.q: Can I use a surcharging tool for my online store?
faq.a: It depends on the tool. GoDaddy Rate Saver, for example, is available for in-person transactions only — it does not apply to ecommerce. Some other processors offer online surcharging capabilities, but ecommerce surcharging has additional complexity around checkout UX, state law, and card network rules. If online surcharging is important to you, confirm your processor's specific capabilities before signing up.

faq.q: What happens if I surcharge in a state where it's not allowed?
faq.a: You could face state enforcement action, customer complaints, and card network violations — which can result in fines or loss of your ability to accept that card brand. It's not worth the risk. If you're in Connecticut or Massachusetts, explore cash-discount programs instead, which may still be permissible — but confirm with a legal advisor.

faq.q: How much can I actually save by passing fees to customers?
faq.a: If you're currently paying 2.3% on $15,000/month in credit card sales, that's $345/month in processing fees. With a compliant surcharging program, that cost shifts to your customers and your effective cost drops toward zero on credit transactions. Debit transactions still carry a cost — GoDaddy Rate Saver charges 1.9% + $0 on debit in-person. Your actual savings depend on your credit-to-debit transaction mix.

faq.q: Will surcharging hurt my business or drive customers away?
faq.a: Research and merchant experience vary. In industries where surcharging is common — gas stations, medical offices, some service businesses — customers are accustomed to it. In retail and food service, it's less universal and some customers do react negatively. The key factors are: clear upfront disclosure, offering a surcharge-free alternative (cash or debit), and the competitive context of your local market. Test it and monitor customer feedback before committing long-term.

faq.q: Do I need special software or hardware to run a surcharging program?
faq.a: Your POS or payment processor needs to support surcharging natively — it should automatically calculate and display the fee at checkout and handle the network registration process. GoDaddy Rate Saver is built into GoDaddy Payments for eligible in-person merchants. If your current processor doesn't support surcharging, you'd need to switch processors or add a compliant surcharging add-on — manual surcharging without proper system support creates compliance and reconciliation risks.
